subject: Benchmark bootstrapping & prompt ownership — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Klein <jk@acme-retail.com>, ops@acme-retail.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-10T15:05:00Z
Subject: Benchmark bootstrapping & prompt ownership — next steps

Hi Jordan / Acme team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to hear the streaming checkout use case in detail. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned before we start any reproducibility work: 

- SLO targets you confirmed on the call: 95th p99 latency <= 180ms for single-turn text completions (avg seq length ~60 tokens), sustained throughput target 120 requests/sec, streaming steady-state concurrent streams target = 80.
- Key constraints: tail-latency sensitivity (peak shopping hours), must be able to reproduce runs in our lab before any Dedicated commitment, and the eval harness should preserve your tokenization/response post-processing.

Immediate asks from our side to bootstrap the benchmark: 
1) Prompt samples (representative prompt families + expected canonical responses) — ideally a CSV with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_response_brief, tokenization_notes.
2) Representative traffic profile (percentiles for sequence length, arrival pattern — e.g., 60% short, 30% medium, 10% long; peak QPS windows).
3) Any existing client-side streaming behavior (chunk sizes, flush frequency) and SDK versions.

If you can drop a small prompt sample CSV and a short note on streaming behavior we can draft a measurement spec and reproduce your scenario in our harness. Proposed timeline: we can produce a first-pass measurement_spec_draft within 3 business days of receiving artifacts, then schedule a short engineering sync to clarify seeds and determinism options.

Thanks —
Marissa
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: acme_prompt_samples.csv (placeholder — please upload a few dozen rows)
From: Jordan Klein <jk@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acme-retail.com
Date: 2028-02-12T16:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Benchmark bootstrapping & prompt ownership — next steps

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. I've attached a trimmed prompt set (acme_prompt_samples.csv) with 45 rows — covers our common checkout dialogues and a handful of edge cases. A couple clarifications:

- The "expected_response_brief" column is intentionally fuzzy; we want human-like variation, but we flagged the canonical intent and a few hard constraints (e.g., do not reveal PII).
- Streaming behavior: we chunk updates every ~120ms on our client (Node SDK v2.1.3), typical chunk size ~16 tokens; we can provide a recording of a 10-minute session if that helps.
- Traffic: peak windows are 18:00–20:00 PST, arrival pattern is bursty (spikes to ~250rps for 60s, then drops). Sustained traffic for qualification should be the 120rps figure we discussed.

We'd like your measurement spec to include how you'll handle stochastic outputs in evaluation (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE not sufficient; we expect intent-level matching + safety checks). Also confirm that the harness can reproduce the streaming flush cadence.

Happy to hop on a 30-min engineer-level call next week if needed.

—Jordan
Jordan Klein
Sr. Engineering Manager, Checkout Experience
Acme Retail
jk@acme-retail.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-13T09:42:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Benchmark bootstrapping & prompt ownership — follow technical questions

Forwarding Acme's prompt sample and initial asks. Monica — can you review and call out any blockers for reproducing their streaming scenario in our harness? A few things I want clarified in our measurement_spec_draft:

- Determinism: do we seed sampling (top-k/top-p) for baseline reproducibility runs or run with natural randomness and measure distributional properties? Recommend we support both: a seeded deterministic run for latency/concurrency baselines, and a stochastic run to capture quality variability.
- Tokenization parity: confirm we run the same tokenizer (we should adopt their SPA tokenization flags if provided).
- Streaming semantics: we need to model client-side 120ms flush cadence. Can our harness emit partial token events and measure end-to-end latency (time-to-first-chunk and time-to-final-token)?

I've attached a draft measurement spec (measurement_spec_draft.pdf) with proposed KPI definitions (time-to-first-byte, time-to-first-chunk, p95/p99 tail-latency, failure/retry accounting) and a suggested reproducibility checklist (deterministic seed, model version pin, synthetic workload generator config).

If there are no blockers, let's aim to run a deterministic baseline next Wednesday (2028-02-15) in our lab and share results by Friday.

Thanks —
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: 2028-02-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Benchmark bootstrapping & prompt ownership — next steps (timeline + canary run)

Jordan —

Perfect, thanks for the CSV and traffic notes. Quick confirmation and proposed plan: 

- We'll perform two canonical runs in our harness: 
  * Deterministic baseline (seeded sampling) focused on latency/concurrency measurement — target date: 2028-02-15 (engineering run in our private lab).
  * Stochastic quality sweep (production-like sampling) to evaluate intent match and safety heuristics — target date: 2028-02-17.

- Deliverables after the deterministic run: raw latency traces, per-route p95/p99, per-token CPU/GPU utilization snapshots, and a reproducibility log (model binary + seed + harness config).
- We'll include measurement_spec_draft.pdf as the working doc; please flag any changes to KPI definitions or safety checks by EOD Monday so we can lock the baselines.

Next steps for you: upload the 10-min streaming recording if available and drop any tokenization flags to the Drive folder (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-benchmark). We'll create a HubSpot activity (deal link: https://hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2028-07) and tag the engineering run.

If that timeline works, Ben and Monica will run the deterministic pass today and I’ll share an initial readout later this week. Thanks again — excited to get this reproducible.

Best,
Marissa

marissa_cole@redwood.ai
